Quite an impressive update by @reya_xyz.

They’ve integrated @Polymarket odds into Reya Agentic, allowing traders to build automated trading strategies around real-world events.

You can now pick a Polymarket event, set an odds threshold, and tell Reya what trade to execute when it’s crossed.

For example:

"Sell 20% of my $BTC holdings on Reya's DEX if Polymarket’s odds of a Fed rate increase in December surge above 50%"

Once you’ve set up your rule, you can see exactly what will trigger a trade and what order Reya will submit (you approve the rule once).

You can also set a max loss before you let it run. If the strategy hits that limit, Reya closes its open positions and stops it.

Polymarket is just the first of many external data sources. In the future, you'll be able to build strategies around a combination of odds, sentiment, posts, and prices from other trading venues.

In the meantime, if you want to try it too, you can join the waitlist here: https://app.reya.xyz/

I know DeSci has seemed pretty dead and quiet lately, but this looks like an interesting unlock:

SEC staff just issued a no-action letter for Molecule's Coin-to-Company model.

early-stage biotech has been stuck in the valley of death for decades, because traditional grant and VC rails are too slow.

now there's a first US template for funding real science with tokens first and bridging to equity later. it puts one of onchain's superpowers to work where it matters: capital formation.

not saying DeSci is back. but precisely because it looks completely dead, it might be worth a closer look again.

THE DAILY METALS PULSE ⚡ | ASIA CLOSE • NOV 26, 2026  
#Uranium #Silver #Gold #Copper

Silver came within 12 cents of $42 in Asia, gold approached $3,600, and Brent traded above $95. For metals investors, oil may be the most important price on the screen today.

🌏 Asian stocks rallied after investors learned that Washington’s proposed tariffs on 14 trading partners would replace the July rates where applicable. That eased fears of a double hit to trade. Meanwhile, South Korea raised its policy rate to 3.25% and lifted its 2027 growth forecast from 2.9% to 4.1% as chip exports boomed.

🥈 Spot silver rose 1.6% to $41.88 and gold gained 0.3% to $3,591 by 05:12 GMT. A softer dollar helped. The question for London is whether silver can trade above $42 and stay there with U.S. investors away for Thanksgiving.

🔌 Copper tells a more cautious story about industrial demand. Shanghai’s January contract fell 2.2% overnight. The premium buyers pay for copper already in Yangshan warehouses also fell $20 to $320 a tonne. If the tariff relief is going to help copper, I’d like to see that premium stabilise alongside futures.

☢️ Uranium’s latest indicative spot reading was just under $90/lb on Wednesday. Australian uranium miners rallied Thursday, and Toronto is open today. I’m watching whether Canadian miners join the move while the underlying fuel price stays near $90.

🛢️ Brent rose to $95.25 after the Houthis said they had attacked a Saudi refinery. The supply impact is still uncertain. What matters for metals is whether oil holds above $95 long enough to push inflation expectations and bond yields higher again. With silver near $42 and gold near $3,600, both have ground to defend when U.S. markets reopen Friday.

Follow @Swedish_Uranium for the next Daily Metals Pulse.

🚨NEW EPISODE🚨

Last Thurs, Joachim Klement – Head of Strategy at @PanmureLiberum – issued a bold note titled
“This Is It: Why I’m Selling”.

He then sold all his equities. It was a great short term call, will it be long term? He joined me yesterday, six days on from the call to test his thesis:

- “I think that we are heading towards a major bear market with more than 30% drawdown risk”
- Falling below 200 day moving average was the key trigger
- Why 200dma isn’t always great timing tool, but why he’s putting so much behind it this time
- Why the bounce on Monday that failed to regain the 200dma has strengthened his conviction
- Key dates and levels to watch from here for SP500 and 200dma
- “You cannot ignore price momentum. No matter how much of a value guy you are, you can't just stand on the tracks and see a train coming towards you and say, 'well, eventually that train has to stop.' Yeah, eventually it has, but until then you could be dead.”
- AI capex growth slowing
- Anthropic revenue growth slowing
- Analyst estimates still complacently confident
- “So my conviction that AI is a bubble is the highest that I've had any conviction in the last 30 years. The question about when is it going to burst…is that it will burst either in 2027 or 2028. And over the last week or two I think if you want to put it on a scale from 1 to 10, my conviction is a 7 or 8, that it is going to burst now or in early 2027.”
- Why he likes 10 year inflation linked US bond and FTSE100 as alternatives

tweets.text:
Have we seen the bottom? We will only know in hindsight. None of us will time it correctly.

But these are definitely tradable bottoms. When the Nasdaq is already down 16% and opens another 4% lower for no apparent reason, you have to be buying something.

If you read my 2025 year-end review and outlook for 2026, I expected low to negative returns from the Nasdaq for the very same reason I believe it will rise meaningfully in 2027.

2026 is the year of AI infrastructure investment. I believe 2027 is when the hyperscalers will start monetizing those investments and generating meaningful profits.

My shopping list for 2027 is as follows:

First tier: $AMZN, $SPCX, $META

Second tier: $GOOG, $MSFT, $NVDA

Third tier (speculative): $ORCL
tweets.quoted_tweet_text:
Keep cool. This too shall pass.

Tech earnings may not be entirely sustainable, but when technology companies trade well below their historical multiples, with some trading at just 3x earnings, you have a substantial margin of safety even if those earnings are overstated.

Right now, the market seems to be treating the entire tech sector as one giant fraud.

There have been very few instances in recent history when selling into this level of fear would have left you better off 12 months later. One of them was the GFC, when the financial system itself was on the verge of collapse.

Many of the companies I am looking at today offer a valuation cushion that simply wasn’t there going into the GFC.

Hold the line.

SPX average returns 12 month out below.

BREAKING NEWS🚨: 7 months ago, NVIDIA’s former and current CEO, Jensen, said that TPU & Trainium would never come to InferenceX to prove their performance claims. Today, we are happy to announce that both Trainium & TPU are on InferenceX/AgentX, the industry standard for inference benchmarking.

ALERT🚨🚨: TokenSpeed pushes Muse Spark Open on @AIatAMD MI355X out to 645 tok/s/user P90 interactivity on the official SemiAnalysis InferenceX AgentX benchmark. At the throughput end, it reaches 48.9K total tok/s per GPU at conc 40 on 4× MI355X.
The AMD and @lightseekorg teams cut latency at every layer of the stack!!

Great work to the AMD and tokenspeed enginer for building all of this in the open on Triton/Gluon and Iris and upstreaming it into TokenSpeed.  Check inferencex for more results! https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/infx/inference/muse-spark-open
